# Pip v4: build guide (generated by `python -m rnd.build_guide`)

**First build:** about **23 h hands-on** (ESTIMATE), plus about **325 h of unattended P2S printing** (13.8 kg PETG/ASA). Reconfiguring later: an arm cartridge swap is 6 × M4 screws with the belt on (~3 min); an arm comes off with one V-band clamp.
**One arm** (the first milestone build): about **5.6 h** hands-on (6.05 → 5.63 h, -25 min, since the last guide), plus ≈ 84 h of printing.

Parts: [BOM](rnd/BOM_v4.md) · M1 kit: [M1_BENCH_ARM.md](M1_BENCH_ARM.md) · prints: [print plan](rnd/print_plan.md) · wiring: [electrical](rnd/electrical.md) · checks: [assembly](rnd/assembly.md), [sim](rnd/sim.md)

| Step | What | Count | Min each | Hours |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Print | Print the parts in print_plan.md order: the bolted cans, rear caps and Oldham adapters first in ASA (they let you bench-test motors early) | 1 | 0 | 0.0 |
| 2 Coupons | Print + test the bolted-flange coupon (6 × M4 inserts, centring lip, Oldham tongue on the bought disc) and the GIM bolt-circle coupon; adjust the flange / tongue / bolt circles in rnd/parts before mass printing | 1 | 45 | 0.8 |
| 3 KX sockets | D15 screwed socket, lift + head pan + tilt only (D24: the arm has none): 6 dowels, 6 coil springs, collar, retainer (3 × M3 into inserts); 3 balls into the male face with retaining compound | 3 | 8 | 0.4 |
| 4a Bolted cartridges | D24: 9 heat-set inserts (6 × M4 in the flange, 3 × M3 in the rim); motor into the sleeve from the rear, rear cap (3 × M3 to the motor + 3 radial M3); Oldham tongue adapter on the output (4 × M3); label + CAN ID (pitch, roll, yaw, elbow × 2) | 8 | 9 | 1.2 |
| 4b Wrist cartridges | D24: DM-J4310 into its can, bolted can flange and output flange (inserts + 6 × M3 each); label + CAN ID | 2 | 9 | 0.3 |
| 4c KX + servo cartridges | Wheels ×4 + lift: motor into its can (3 screws), torque pin, KX adapter (4 screws); STS3215 sleeves ×6 | 11 | 6 | 1.1 |
| 5 Belt stages | D13 v3 + D19: 6801s into the eccentric bushings, Ø12 shaft through wall A, aluminium pulley, wall B; Oldham clamp hub on the shaft end + disc; the one-piece shaft-pulley with its bearings into the capped U-slots, caps on (2 × M4 / M3); belt on, tension with the bushings; cartridge nose into the counterbore, 6 × M4 countersunk from the pulley side (the lift keeps its KX74 stage) | 9 | 14 | 2.1 |
| 5b Clock springs | Wind the 6 ribbon cassettes per arm (D14 ribbon) and fit them at pitch, roll, yaw, elbow, wrist pitch, wrist roll | 2 | 30 | 1.0 |
| 6 Arms | Bond the CF tubes into the sockets (epoxy, cure overnight); upper bone + elbow cassette (in from below, seat caps), forearm + clamp (2 × M5), wrist + hand + gripper, roll/yaw module | 2 | 90 | 3.0 |
| 7 Shoulders | Pitch modules: bracket body, one-piece pitch shaft, outer wall (3 × M4), pitch hub, balancer (die spring, cord, pulley A at the 40–60 mm slot), V-band ferrule | 2 | 45 | 1.5 |
| 8 Mast + torso + head | Ratchet strip segments, lift drive + belt, carriage (8 × 625), torso halves around the carriage, head bracket + pan/tilt + shell | 1 | 150 | 2.5 |
| 9 Base | 4 wheel modules (pods, shafts, hubs, wheels), deck quarters, skirt, coupling, battery bay, lidar, electronics | 1 | 120 | 2.0 |
| 10 Wiring | Pre-made daisy-chain harness segments (JST-GH CAN/TTL, VH power) per module; power distribution board; detach plugs | 1 | 120 | 2.0 |
| 10b Sensors (D9) | Joint-side encoder magnets + boards (9), fingertip tactile pads (4), palm ToF (2), cliff ToF (4), 3 RP2040 CAN sensor nodes | 1 | 160 | 2.7 |
| 11 Bring-up | sw/bringup.py per arm (enumerate, drive limits to flash, e-stop + watchdog, hard-stop zeroing, 10 % jog, gravity hold); balancer K from the fit, lift pawl test, regen clamp test | 1 | 120 | 2.0 |
| | **Total hands-on** | | | **22.5** |

**Wave 1 (D24 bolted cartridges, D19):** sockets + cartridges 3.8 → 3.0 h for the robot; one arm 6.05 → 5.63 h (-25 min). The 5 D15 sockets per arm go (−40 min); the bolted cartridges' 9 heat-set inserts and the Oldham adapter take about half of that back. D19's one-piece shaft-pulleys replace the split pulleys (no keyed joint to fit) at about the same time, the seat-cap screws included.

**Against R10** (first build ≤ 4 h): **not met.**
- **Loop 10 cut the estimate from 25 h to ~19 h:**
    - print-in-place KX sockets with pins and spring embedded at print pauses (no retainer, no screws) — *retired in loop 40 (D15): the screwed socket takes ≈ 8 min; D24 then removed the sockets from the arm*
    - 7 instead of 14 screws per cartridge
    - eccentric-bushing belt tensioning
    - pre-made harness segments
- **A 21-actuator robot won't reach 4 h.** Precedent: a 6-servo LeRobot SO-101 arm takes a few hours.
- **Proposed target split (owner decision):** first build of one arm ≤ 4 h; whole robot ≤ 15 h; any module swap ≤ 5 min.

## Safety notes
- 24 V Li-ion: use the specified BMS (≥ 30 A), fuse every branch, and charge on a non-flammable surface.
- The arms can pinch. Torque limits are set in the drives (bring-up step 2, saved to flash) and bounded again by the safety supervisor. The bolted arm cartridges have **no mechanical slip backstop** (the KX seats slipped at ≈ 1.16× peak); only the lift and head sockets still do.
- Test the lift pawl, the e-stop and the watchdog (sw/bringup.py step 3) before any powered arm motion; bench work with the catch cradle ≤ 50 mm under the arm.
